nodes.question: What are some ecological benefits provided by legumes when included in rotations?
nodes.answer: Some ecological benefits include improved nitrogen use efficiency, nitrogen credit from biological fixation, increased water conservation, reduced N2O emissions, improved soil health, and enhanced biodiversity.
nodes.paragraph: 2018). The inclu- sion of pulses into simplified rotations is a widely adopted diversification strategy (Hufnagel et al. 2020), as legumes can provide an array of ecological benefits (Ditzler et al. 2021). Some examples are improved N use efficiency (St. Luce et al. 2015), N credit from biological fixation (Bell et al. 2017; Taveira et al. 2020), increased water conserva- tion (Gan et al. 2017; Seymour et al. 2012), reduced N2O emissions (Lemke et al. 2007; Liu et al. 2024), improved soil health (Lal 2017), and enhanced biodiversity (Zander et al. 2016). These valuable ecosystem services encourage farmers to include pulse crops into cereal and oilseed rotations, par - ticularly in semi-arid cropping systems, where limited water availability presents significant challenges to sustainability. Canada leads global lentil and pea production, yielding 2.9 million tonnes of lentils and 4.6 million tonnes of peas in 2021, which accounts for 45% and 31% of world produc - tion (FAO 2024).

nodes.label: Facts
nodes.question: What economic benefits can be derived from incorporating pulse crops into wheat-based rotations in the Canadian prairies?
nodes.answer: Incorporating pulse crops into wheat-based rotations in the semi-arid Canadian prairies led to economic benefits for producers.
nodes.paragraph: The Canadian prairies contribute to 98% of the Canadian pea and lentil production (Saskatchewan Pulse Growers 2024). In addition, incorporating pulse crops in wheat-based rotations in the semi-arid Canadian prairies led to economic benefits for producers (Khakbazan et al. 2022). In the semi-arid Canadian prairies, where water is the most limited yield factor, simplified cropping systems negatively impact both non-legume and pulse crop produc- tion, as well as the ecological benefits associated with pulse crops. Therefore, a comprehensive evaluation using multiple indicators collectively is needed on ecosystem services in response to diversification of crop rotations with pulse crops, particularly at the cropping system level in the intermediate term (e.g., 5 10 years). Synergies and trade-offs among ecosystem services are widely recognized and reported in cropping systems (Power 2010 ; Rodr guez et al. 2006 ). However, most studies have often focused on individual ecosystem services, although sustainable cropping systems require a holistic improve- ment in ecosystem services, including crop productivity, resource use efficiency, economic returns, soil health, and environmental health.

nodes.question: Name two practices involved in sustainable agriculture that contribute to soil health and biodiversity.
nodes.answer: Crop rotation and agroforestry are two practices involved in sustainable agriculture that contribute to soil health and enhance biodiversity.
nodes.paragraph: Sustainable agriculture Sustainable agriculture represents a holistic approach to farming, aiming to meet current food needs without compromising the ability of future generations to meet theirs(Altieri et al. 2017 ; Gomiero et al. 2011 ; Kout - souris 2009 ; Lichtfouse et al. 2009 ; Mason 2003 ; Muhie 2022 ; Rajput et al. 2023 , 2024 ; Velten et al. 2015 ). It inte - grates three primary goals: environmental health, eco - nomic profitability, and social equity(Chen et al. 2021 ; Czy ewski and Kryszak 2022 ; D nmez et al. 2024 ; Velten et al. 2015 ). Practices such as crop rotation, agroforestry, and organic farming play a pivotal role in maintain - ing soil health, reducing erosion, and enhancing biodiversity(Lekberg et al. 2024 ; Ngaba et al. 2024 ; Tully and McAskill 2020 ). By optimizing resource use and minimizing reliance on nonrenewable inputs, sustainable agriculture ensures long-term profitability(D nmez et al. 2024 ).
